DIVINE cohort

  • Adult patients hospitalized

  • SARS-CoV-2 infection

  • 5 centers and 4 waves

  • South metropolitan area of Barcelona

  • Data stored in REDCap

\(\longrightarrow\) Make data available to support reproducible research and to enable its reuse

Purposes

  • Support education

  • Validate existing predictive models

  • Analyze the data

    • Clinical characteristics

    • Outcomes incidence

    • Prognostic factors

DIVINE package

DIVINE package

The DIVINE package contains:

  • 14 datasets for 5813 patients

  • 6 data management functions: inspect, clean, merge, summarize, visualize, and export data efficiently

DIVINE Datasets

  • Baseline datasets: demographic, comorbidities, symptoms, vital_signs, analytics, concomitant_medication, scores, and vaccine.

  • Follow-up datasets: icu, complications, inhosp_antivirals, inhosp_other_treatments, inhosp_antibiotics, and end_followup.

Note

Common variables: ID, wave, and center of admission

DIVINE Functions

A total of 6 functions:

  • data_overview()

  • impute_missing()

  • multi_join()

  • stats_table()

  • multi_plot()

  • export_data()

data_overview()

  • Fast snapshot of a data frame.

  • Returns a list with four elements (dimensions, variable_types, missing_values, preview).

data_overview(demographic, preview_rows = 5)

Note

Use early in a script to detect structural issues and NA patterns.

data_overview()

over <- data_overview(demographic, preview_rows = 5)

over$dimensions

impute_missing()

Replace or remove missing values

impute_missing(comorbidities)

Default behavior:

  • Numeric columns: imputed with mean

  • Character/Factor columns: imputed with mode

Tip

Combine with data_overview() to check missingness before and after imputation.

impute_missing()

Numerical variables:

cleaned <- impute_missing(
  comorbidities,
  method = list(
    weight ~ "mean",
    height ~ "median",
    type_dm ~ "Unknown"
  )
)

List of missing values (before):

 weight  height type_dm 
   1274    1475    4461

List of missing values (after):

 weight  height type_dm 
      0       0       0

multi_join()

Sequentially join multiple datasets.

  • join_type supports left, inner, full, right.
multi_join(
  list(analytics, scores),
  join_type = "left"
)

multi_join()

Sequentially join multiple datasets.

  • join_type supports left, inner, full, right.
joined <- multi_join(
  list(analytics, scores, icu, symptoms),
  key = c("record_id", "covid_wave", "center"),
  join_type = "left"
)

Dimensions (before):

analytics : 5813 × 9 
scores : 5813 × 10 
icu : 5813 × 14 
symptoms : 5813 × 24

Dimensions (after):

joined: 5813 × 48

stats_table()

Build publication-ready tables using {gtsummary}.

  • statistic_type = "mean_sd", "median_iqr", or "both".
stats_table(
  vital_signs,
  vars = c("temperature", "normal_radio"),
  statistic_type = "both"
)
Variables N = 5,813
Temperature
    Mean (SD) 36.96 (0.96)
    Median [Q1;Q3] 36.80 [36.20;37.60]
    Unknown 102
Normal X-ray, n (%) 463 (8.05%)
    Unknown 64

stats_table()

Stratified by a variable.

stats_table(
  vital_signs,
  vars = c("temperature", "normal_radio"),
  statistic_type = "both",
  by = "supporto2"
)

multi_plot()

  • Single entrypoint for histograms, boxplots, density plots, scatter, spider (radar), etc.

  • Returns a ggplot2 or plotly object.

multi_plot(
  demographic,
  x = "age",
  plot_type = "histogram"
)

Note

This function already applies a default theme using theme_minimal() from {ggplot2}

multi_plot()

Boxplot

multi_plot(
  demographic,
  x = "sex",
  y = "age",
  plot_type = "boxplot",
  fill_color = 
    c("darkgreen","purple")
)

multi_plot()

Spider plot

multi_plot(
  comorbidities,
  radar = c("hypertension",
            "dyslipidemia",
            "dm", 
            "mild_kidney_disease", 
            "chronic_lung_disease"),
  radar_labels = c("Hypertension",
                    "Dyslipidemia",
                    "Diabetes",
                    "Mild CKD",
                    "COPD"),
  plot_type = "spider"
)

export_data()

Save a dataset to CSV, Excel, RData, Rdata, SPSS, Stata or SAS.

export_data(cleaned, path = "cleaned_icu.csv")
export_data(cleaned, path = "cleaned_icu_2025-12-04_v1", format = "txt")

Tip

File naming: include date and a short tag, e.g. joined_2025-12-04_v1.xlsx.

Further information

You can visit the {DIVINE} website: https://bruigtp.github.io/DIVINE/

Discussion

Discussion

  • The DIVINE R package provides 14 datasets and 6 functions

  • Data includes variables commonly used in longitudinal and hospital-based analyses:

    • Validating predictive models, outcome incidence and prognostic factors

    • Teaching resource in biostatistics or epidemiology

  • Functions can be used to inspect, clean, merge, summarize, visualize, and export data

Thank you!
